root_idea.summary: Forceful, unhesitating entry into something difficult, perilous, or resistant.
root_idea.development: The root develops from plunging forward into affairs or formidable obstacles to related ideas of difficult passages, forceful movement, specialized camel and horse usages, disputes that drive a person into an unwanted course, and deprivation that drives people onward. These extensions describe the root's orientation and are not meanings of every Quranic form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested active participle is presented as its own public form.

senses.definition: To plunge into the midst of a frightening hardship; to undertake a formidable or perilous obstacle.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for forceful entry into a difficult or dangerous matter. The Quranic construction اقتحم العقبة presents the obstacle as something formidable to be undertaken; contextual renderings such as “attempted” and “bursting” reflect this same lexical use.

senses.definition: One who plunges into or bursts into a frighteningly difficult or perilous situation.
senses.usage_conditions: Active-participial designation of a person or group entering a formidable situation; the Quranic usage in هذا فوج مقتحم portrays a group as entering into such severity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw oneself into an affair, or plunge or rush into it, without consideration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic usage of the Form I and Form V derivatives, emphasizing rash entry into an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To experience dearth, drought, or sterility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form V usage referring to undergoing conditions of scarcity or barrenness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Redundant or foisted in; a word or letter inserted without reason.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an unnecessary word or letter in textual or grammatical description.
